Hi Stan,

I have some further information: the python console displays the following error message when the memory access violation occurs:

_Incorrect number of arguments passed to called function!
  call void @llvm.memcpy.p5i8.p0i8.i64(i8 addrspace(5)* align 4 %bitCast3, i8* align 4 %scevgep.i10.i, i64 24, i1 false) #2

I hope this sounds familiar to you.  It seems to me that this is really compilation time errors, since not a line is executed from the code (not even the first print command).
I managed somehow to track down which part of the code is the problematic one: my kernel function calls a device function and there I try to retrieve a value from a big constant array (with a total size of 161 021 952 bytes):
_shape = (252, 64, 3, 2 * 2* 2* 2* 2* 2, 13), dtype=numpy.float32_

This array is initialized and uploaded to the GPU with the help of the cuda.to_device() function prior to the kernel invocation, and its content doesn't change during the kernel run, so it is constant.

This is the line which causes the problem in the device function:

envTotal = myArray [index, upperTotalValue, slotVal, ind, action]

My guesses are:
- either the array is too big
- or the number of 5 indices are too much

What do you think?
Thanks imn advance,
Ferenc
that is an excellent bit of debugging.  @sklam: Is there an index limit on the GPU?  Is it possible we're hitting some argument count limit when the array arguments are unpacked?

I can't replicate the problem.  Compilation shouldn't be affected by big array.

I think this might be a LLVM compatibility problem; i.e. our LLVM8 vs NVVM.  This is likely an issue with `llvm.memcpy` having a different API. But, we shouldn't be generating memcpy calls. No GPU features should be emitting that.  

Is it possible to provide a minimal reproducer?

Hi,
It took me about two weeks to amend my code in order to get rid of the Memory Access Violation errors of the llvm lite compiler. I have to emphasize again that all these error appear in compile time, so no code is executed. My code is complex, consists of more than thousand lines with many device side functions and preloaded constant arrays into the GPU memory. Now, having managed to get rid of the errors I have some availability so I will try my best to create short code which reproduces the errors. What I figured out were as follows:

0.) I didn't use function signatures, because I could not figure out how to exactly define them when using custom types (see below). 

1.) Cuda & llvm combo doesn't like if I pack multiple arrays of constant values into a custom type array and try to copy from these content into local arrays within a device function. 

What I did: in order to speed up computation I have calculated in advance some constant values in form of 10 different numpy arrays. In order to load them into the GPU memory I declared a custom type which packs all 10 arrays into a structure, so I can pass as parameter to the various device functions only the this variable  of custom type (and I don't need to pass reference to all ten of them). 

cuda_const_arrays_type = numpy.dtype([
    ('a1', (numpy.int32,(7776, 13))),
    ('a2', (numpy.int32,(7776, 2, 5))),
    ('a3', (numpy.int32,(16494592))),
    ('a4', (numpy.int32,13)),
    ('a5', (numpy.float32,(22528, 64))),
    ('a6', (numpy.int32,(522523, 64))),
    ('a7', (numpy.int32,(32,5))),
    ('a8', (numpy.int32,(66667))),
    ('a9', (numpy.int32,(252, 64, 3, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 13))),
    ('a10', (numpy.int32,(7776)))
    ])

Then I defined the variable on host side:

cuda_const_arrays = numpy.zeros(1, dtype=cuda_const_arrays_type)
# .. load each array separately from disc and store them into the cuda_const_arrays[0]['a1'], cuda_const_arrays[0]['a2'], .... cuda_const_arrays[0]['a10'] respectively
# load the packed array to the device
gpu_const_arrays = cuda.to_device(cuda_const_arrays[0])

As a result within a device function I could access any member of this arrays:
@cuda.jit(device=True)
def cuda_doSomething(gpu_const_arrays,...):
...
       arrayOfSize13 = gpu_const_arrays.a1[index]
 ...
Now when I copied data from this constant arrays into some local array of a device function:
actions = cuda.local.array(13, numba.int32)
...
     for i in range(13):
          actions [i] = arrayOfSize13 [i]

and tried to use it later in the same device function, like
      v = actions [i] *2

This led to Memory access violation in the compiler on a random basis. Finally I got rid of the packed constant array and defined & loaded each of them separately to the device. 

2.) Device function code length

I observed that for some reason if the device function contains relatively many lines (e.g. 100), it also causes problem to the compiler. Thus I had to reorganize code and create more device function-type subroutines.

3.) The llvm compiler identifies some of the non-python elements extremely slow. For example I wanted to print out stack trace (which turned out finally that it is unsupported )
import traceback
...
       traceback.print_stack()
On my computer it takes about one hour till the compiler returns that this is unsupported feature. Similar case with import sys and sys.exit().


As mentioned above, I will try to reproduce these and let you know.
